props.title: Music that gets out of the way of the speeches.
props.lede: The speeches are the point of a retirement party, so the music is built around them: silent for the remarks, back the moment the glass goes down, and sized to the place.

rows.term: The jazz duo, or one guitar
rows.text: Upright bass and guitar, or one jazz guitarist, playing the standards quietly under the dinner. The standards reach a table of colleagues aged twenty-five to seventy at once, and the jazz duo stops for every speech.

Standards and the songs from the retiree’s own decades, played through cocktails and dinner on the venue’s piano or on a stage piano we bring. A solo pianist fits a restaurant’s private dining space as easily as a club.
One voice and a guitar playing the songs the office knows and the one the retiree has always asked for, learned for the night. Tejas Singh plays it.

rows.term: Live band karaoke for the department
rows.text: The band plays the 80s and 90s hits on its own and hands the microphone to the colleagues who’ve been threatening to sing for a decade. The retiring colleague’s one karaoke song is a request we take the week before. Live band karaoke needs a big private space or a hotel event space.

A trio or a quartet for the send-off that ends on a floor. Tony Medina plays it up to a four piece, the same band plays the dinner first, and the DJ can take the late end through the same sound system.

items.q: Can we hire a band for a retirement party?
items.a: Yes. Most start with a jazz duo or one guitarist under the dinner, a singer with a guitar plays the retiree's song, live band karaoke gets the department singing, and a trio or a quartet plays the send-off that dances. It's one contract with one personal contact, booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

items.q: How does the music work around the speeches?
items.a: The duo plays at the level of the conversation, stops for each speech and comes back the moment the glass goes down, and an announcement microphone is live for whoever stands up. Tell us roughly when the speeches fall and the set is built around them.

items.q: Can the company pay by purchase order?
items.a: Yes. A company's retirement dinner is booked like any corporate event: vendor setup, a purchase order, a certificate of insurance and a W-9 are all available. Procurement is rarely fast, so start early.

items.q: How much space does the band need in a private dining space?
items.a: One guitar takes about 6 by 4 feet on one circuit, a duo 8 by 6, a trio 12 by 8, and a quartet or live band karaoke 14 by 10 on two circuits, with karaoke's two lyric screens. Setup runs 45 minutes for a solo and an hour for a duo or a trio, and we settle setup, power and volume with the venue before the day.

props.title: Send us the date, the place and who's throwing it.
